# BAB I

## KETENTUAN UMUM

#### Pasal 1

Dalam Peraturan Daerah ini, yang dimaksud dengan:

1. Kabupaten adalah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
2. Pemerintah Kabupaten adalah Pemerintah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
3. Bupati adalah Bupati Ogan Komering Ulu.  
4. Perangkat Daerah yang selanjutnya disingkat PD adalah Perangkat Daerah di Lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu.  
5. Gender adalah konsep yang mengacu pada pembedaan peran dan tanggung jawab laki-laki dan perempuan yang terjadi akibat dari dan dapat berubah oleh keadaan sosial dan budaya masyarakat.  
6. Kesetaraan Gender yang selanjutnya disingkat KG adalah kesamaan kondisi bagi laki-laki dan perempuan untuk memperoleh kesempatan dan hak-haknya sebagai manusia, agar mampu berperan dan berpartisipasi dalam kegiatan politik, ekonomi, sosial budaya, pertahanan dan keamanan dan kesamaan dalam menikmati hasil pembangunan.  
7. Analisis Gender adalah proses yang dibangun secara sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi dan memahami pembagian kerja atau peran laki-laki dan perempuan, akses, dan kontrol terhadap sumber-sumber daya pembangunan, partisipasi dalam proses pembangunan dan manfaat yang mereka nikmati.  
8. Pengarusutamaan Gender yang selanjutnya disingkat PUG adalah strategi yang dibangun untuk mengintegrasikan gender menjadi satu dimensi integral -3- dari perencanaan, penyusunan, pelaksanaan, pemantauan, dan evaluasi atas kebijakan, program dan kegiatan pembangunan di daerah.  
9. Responsif gender adalah suatu kebijakan, program, kegiatan, dan penganggaran yang memperkecil perbedaan, kebutuhan, pengalaman, dan aspirasi laki-laki dan perempuan.  
10. Anggaran Responsif Gender selanjutnya disingkat ARG adalah anggaran yang respon terhadap kebutuhan perempuan dan laki-laki yang tujuan untuk mewujudkan kesetaraan dan keadilan gender.  
11. Pemberdayaan perempuan adalah upaya perempuan untuk memperoleh akses dan kontrol terhadap sumber daya, ekonomi, politik, sosial, budaya, agar perempuan dapat mengatur diri dan meningkatkan rasa percaya diri untuk mampu berperan dan berpartisipasi aktif dalammemecahkan masalah, sehingga mampu membangun kemampuan dan konsep diri.  
12. Perlindungan perempuan adalah segala upaya yang ditujukan untuk melindungi perempuan dan memberikan rasaaman dalam pemenuhan hak-haknya dengan memberikan perhatian yang konsisten dan sistematis yang ditujukan untuk mencapai kesetaraan gender.  
13. Anak adalah seseorang yang belum berusia 18 (delapanbelas) tahun, termasuk anak yang masih dalamkandungan.  
14. Perlindungan Anak adalah segala kegiatan untuk menjamindan melindungi Anak dan hak-haknya agar dapat hidup, tumbuh, berkembang, dan berpartisipasi secara optimal sesuai dengan harkat dan martabat kemanusiaan, serta mendapat perlindungan dari kekerasan dan diskriminasi.  
15. Perlindungan Khusus adalah suatu bentuk perlindungan yang diterima oleh Anak dalam situasi dan kondisi tertentu untuk mendapatkan jaminan rasa aman terhadap ancaman yang membahayakan diri dan jiwa dalam tumbuh kembangnya.  
16. Kekerasan adalah setiap perbuatan melawan hukum yang berakibat timbulnya kesengsaraan atau penderitaan secarafisik, seksual, mental, psikologis, termasuk penelantaran dan perlakuan buruk yang mengancamdan/atau membahayakan bagi jiwa dan raga serta merendahkan martabat.  
17. Perlindungan Khusus Anak adalah suatu bentuk perlindungan yang diterima oleh anak dalam situasi dan kondisi tertentu untuk mendapatkan jaminan rasa aman terhadap ancaman yang membahayakan diri dan jiwa dalam tubuh kembangnya.  
18. Anak dalam Situasi Darurat adalah Anak yang berada dalam situasi lingkungan yang mengancam dan mengganggu kehidupan dan penghidupan Anak yang -4- disebabkan, baik oleh faktor alam, nonalam, dan/ atau sosial.  
19. Anak yang Berhadapan dengan Hukum adalah Anak yang berkonflik dengan hukum, Anak yang menjadi korban tindak pidana, dan Anak yang menjadi saksi tindak pidana.  
20. Anak dari Kelompok Minoritas dan Terisolasi adalah Anak yang tertinggal, terdepan, terluar dalam lingkungan yang berbeda budaya, tradisi, suku, ras, agama dengan anak- anak lain yang jumlahnya jauh lebih sedikit dari Anak golongan lain.  
21. Anak yang Dieksploitasi secara Ekonomi adalah Anak yang menjadi korban dari tindakan pelacuran, kerja atau pelayanan paksa, perbudakan atau praktik serupa perbudakan, penindasan, pemerasan, pemanfaatan fisik, seksual, organ reproduksi, atau secara melawan hukummemindahkan atau mentransplantasi organ dan/atau jaringan tubuh atau memanfaatkan tenaga atau kemampuan Anak oleh pihak lain atau tindakan lain yang sejenis untuk mendapatkan keuntungan materiil.  
22. Anak yang Dieksploitasi secara Seksual adalah Anak yang dimanfaatkan untuk mendapatkan keuntungan melalui organ tubuh seksual atau organ tubuh lain dari Anak, termasuk tetapi tidak terbatas pada semua kegiatan pelacuran dan pencabulan.  
23. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Penyalahgunaan Narkotika, Alkohol, Psikotropika, dan Zat Adiktif Lainnya adalah Anak yang dibujuk, diperdaya, ditipu, dipaksa, dan/atau diancam untuk menggunakan narkotika, alkohol, psikotropika, dan zat adiktif lainnya.  
24. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Pornografi adalah Anak yang mengalami trauma atau penderitaan sebagai akibat tindak pidana pornografi.  
25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus yang selanjutnya disingkat HIV adalah virus yang menyerang sistem imun dan jika tidak diterapi dapat menurunkan daya tahan tubuh manusia hingga terjadi kondisi Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome.  
26. Acquired Immuno Deficiencg Syndrome yang selanjutnya disingkat AIDS adalah suatu kumpulan gejala berkurangnya kemampuan pertahanan diri yang disebabkan oleh masuknya virus HIV dalam tubuh seseorang.  
27. Anak dengan HIV dan AIDS adalah Anak yang terinfeksi HIV dan/atau AIDS baik tertular dari orang tua ataupun dari faktor risiko lainnya.  
28. Anak Korban Penculikan adalah Anak yang dibawa seseorang secara melawan hukum dengan maksud untuk menempatkan Anak tersebut di bawah kekuasaannya atau kekuasaan orang lain atau untuk menempatkan Anak dalam keadaan tidak berdaya.

29. Anak Korban Penjualan adalah Anak yang dipindahtangankan oleh seseorang atau kelompok orang ke pihak lainnya untuk suatu imbalan atau alasan lainnya.  
30. Anak Korban Perdagangan adalah Anak yang mengalami penderitaan psikis, mental, fisik, seksual, ekonomi, dan/atau sosial yang diakibatkan tindakan perekrutan, pengangkutan, penampungan, pengiriman, pemindahan, atau penerimaan dengan ancaman kekerasan, penggunaan kekerasan, penculikan, penyekapan, pemalsuan, penipuan, penyalahgunaan kekuasaan atau posisi rentan, penjeratan utang atau memberi bayaran atau manfaat, sehingga memperoleh persetujuan dari orang yang memegang kendali atas orang lain tersebut, baik yang dilakukan di dalam negara maupun antarnegara, untuk tujuan eksploitasi atau mengakibatkan Anak tereksploitasi.  
31. Anak Korban Kekerasan Fisik adalah Anak yang mengalami kekerasan yang menimbulkan rasa sakit, jatuh sakit, atau luka berat.  
32. Anak Korban Kekerasan Psikis adalah Anak yang mengalami ketakutan, hilangnya rasa percaya diri, hilangnya kemampuan untuk bertindak, rasa tidak berdaya, dan/atau penderitaan psikis berat.  
33. Anak Korban Kejahatan Seksual adalah Anak yang mengalami pemaksaan hubungan seksual, pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan cara tidak wajar dan/atau tidak disukai, dan pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial dan I atau tujuan tertentu.  
34. Anak Korban Jaringan Terorisme adalah Anak yang mengalami penderitaan fisik, mental, dan/atau kerugian ekonomi yang disebabkan oleh tindak pidana terorisme baik sebagai Anak korban, Anak pelaku, Anak dari pelaku, dan Anak saksi.  
35. Anak Penyandang Disabilitas adalah Anak yang mengalami keterbatasan fisik, intelektual, mental, dan/atau sensorik dalam jangka waktu lama yang dalamberinteraksi dengan lingkungan dapat mengalami hambatan dan kesulitan untuk berpartisipasi secara penuh dan efektif berdasarkan kesamaan hak.  
36. Anak Korban Perlakuan Salah adalah Anak yang terancam secara fisik dan nonfisik karena tindak kekerasan, diperlakukan salah atau tidak semestinya dalam lingkungan keluarga atau lingkungan sosial terdekatnya, sehingga tidak terpenuhi kebutuhan dasarnya dengan wajar baik secara jasmani, rohani, maupun sosial.  
37. Anak Korban Penelantaran adalah Anak yang tidak mendapatkan pemenuhan kebutuhan seperti namun tidak terbatas pada kebutuhan kesehatan, keamanan, dan kesejahteraan dari orang tua atau orang lain yang -6- memiliki tanggung jawab secara hukum untuk mengasuh Anak tersebut sehingga mengakibatkan kerugian dalamproses tumbuh kembang Anak.  
38. Anak dengan Perilaku Sosial Menyimpang adalah Anak yang bersikap dan berperilaku yang tidak mempertimbangkan penilaian dan keberadaan orang lain secara umum di sekitarnya, menunjukkan sikap tidak bertanggung jawab serta kurangnya penyesalan mengenai kesalahannya, dan sering melakukan pelanggaran hak dan norma yang hidup dalam masyarakat.  
39. Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya adalah Anak yang diberikan label sosial negatif didasarkan pada prasangka dan bertujuan untuk memisahkan, membedakan, mendiskreditkan, dan mengucilkan Anak dengan cap atau pandangan buruk dari pelabelan terkait dengan kondisi orang tuanya.  
40. Keluarga Pengganti adalah orang tua asuh, orang tua angkat, dan wali yang menjalankan peran dan tanggung jawab untuk memberikan pengasuhan alternatif pada Anak.  
41. Lembaga Pendidikan adalah satuan pendidikan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam peraturan perundang- undangan mengenai sistem pendidikan nasional.  
42. Konseling adalah suatu proses yang dilakukan dalambentuk wawancara untuk membantu Anak memahami dirinya secara lebih baik, agar Anak dapat mengatasi kesulitan dalam penyesuaian dirinya terhadap berbagai peranan dan relasi serta menemukan pemecahan permasalahan yang tepat.  
43. Pendampingan Sosial adalah interaksi dinamis antara pekerja sosial dengan Anak yang memerlukan Perlindungan Khusus untuk bersama-sama menghadapi dan memecahkan masalah sosial yang dihadapi.  
44. Rehabilitasi Sosial adalah proses refungsionalisasi dan pengembangan untuk memungkinkan Anak mampu melaksanakan fungsi sosialnya secara wajar dalamkehidupan masyarakat.  
45. Reintegrasi Sosial adalah proses penyiapan Anak yang memerlukan Perlindungan Khusus untuk dapat kembali ke lingkungan keluarga dan masyarakat.  
46. Pemenuhan Hak Anak yang selanjutnya disingkat PHA adalah strategi perlindungan anak dengan mengintegrasikan hak anak ke dalam setiap kegiatan pembangunan yang sejak penyusunan perencanaan, penganggaran, pelaksanaan, pemantauan, dan evaluasi dari berbagai peraturan perundang-undangan, kebijakan, program, dan kegiatan dengan menerapkan prinsip kepentingan terbaik bagi anak.  
47. Diskriminasi adalah setiap pembatasan, pelecehan, atau pengucilan, yang secara langsung atau tidak langsung -7- didasarkan pada pembedaan pada manusia atas dasar, agama, suku, ras, golongan, status sosial, status ekonomi, jenis kelamin, bahasa, keyakinan politik, status hukum anak, dan kondisi fisik dan/atau mental yang berakibat pengurangan, penyimpangan, atau penghapusan, pengakuan, pelaksanaan atau penggunaan hak asasi manusia dan kebebasan dasar dalamkehidupan baik individual maupun kolektif dalam bidang politik, ekonomi, hukum, sosial budaya dan aspek kehidupan lainnya.  
48. Eksploitasi adalah tindakan dengan atau tanpa persetujuan korban yang meliputi tetapi tidak terbatas pada pelacuran, kerja atau pelayanan paksa, perbudakan atau praktik serupa perbudakan, penindasan, pemerasan, pemanfaatan fisik seksual, organ reproduksi atau secara melawan hukum memindahkan atau mentransplatasikan organ dan/atau jaringan tubuh atau memanfaatkan tenaga atau kemampuan seseorang oleh pihak lain untuk mendapatkan keuntungan baik materiil maupun immateriil.  
49. Orangtua adalah ayah dan/atau ibu kandung, atau ayah dan/atau ibu tiri, atau ayah dan/atau ibu angkat.  
50. Wali adalah orang atau badan yang dalam kenyataannya menjalankan kekuasaan asuh sebagai orang tua terhadap anak.  
51. Keluarga adalah unit terkecil dalam masyarakat yang terdiri dari suami isteri dan anaknya, atau ayah dan anaknya, atau ibu dan anaknya, atau keluarga sedarah dalam garis lurus ke atas atau ke bawah sampai dengan derajat ketiga.  
52. Masyarakat adalah perseorangan, keluarga, kelompok dan organisasi sosial dan/atau organisasi kemasyarakatan, dunia usaha.

# CHAPTER I

## GENERAL PROVISIONS

#### Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu.  
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.  
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.  
6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.  
7. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy.  
8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region.  
9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women.  
10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice.  
11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.  
12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.  
13. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb.  
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.  
15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.  
16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.  
17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.  
18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children that -4- are caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.  
19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.  
20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.  
21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.  
22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.  
23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.  
24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.  
25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs.  
26. Acquired Immuno Deficiencg Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body.  
27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.  
28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state.

29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons.  
30. Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of Children.  
31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.  
32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.  
33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.  
34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses.

36. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that exist in society.  
39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents.  
40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children.  
41. Educational Institution is an educational unit as referred to in laws and regulations concerning the national education system.

45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment.  
46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child.  
47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, which directly or indirectly -7- is based on differentiation in humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life.  
48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.  
49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.  
50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.  
51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree.  
52. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

# BAB II

## PEMBERDAYAAN PEREMPUAN

## Bagian Kesatu

Umum

#### Pasal 2

( 1 ) Pemberdayaan perempuan di Kabupaten dilaksanakan melalui perlindungan hak perempuan.  

( 2 ) Pemberdayaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan dalam rangka memenuhi hak perempuan dalam meningkatkan kualitas hidup perempuan.  

( 3 ) Hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) wajib dijamin oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten.  
8- ( 4 ) Hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (3) meliputi bidang pendidikan, bidang kesehatan, bidang ketenagakerjaan, bidang politik, bidang hukum, bidang ekonomi budaya dan sosial.

## Bagian Kedua

Kewajiban Pemerintah Kabupaten

#### Pasal 3

( 1 ) Pemerintah Kabupaten wajib menjamin perlindungan hak perempuan.  

( 2 ) Perlindungan hak perempuan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan dengan:
a. penyusunan kebijakan daerah yang responsif gender;  
b. pelembagaan PUG di lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten;  
c. pemberdayaan perempuan di bidang pendidikan, bidang kesehatan, bidang ketenagakerjaan, bidang politik, bidang hukum, bidang ekonomi budaya dan social pada organisasi kemasyarakatan tingkat Kabupaten; dand. penguatan dan pengembangan lembaga penyedia layanan pemberdayaan perempuan tingkat kabupaten.

#### Pasal 4

1. Penyusunan kebijakan Kabupaten yang responsif gender sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf a menjadi pedoman dalam penyusunan rencana pembangunan daerah.  
2. Penyusunan rencana pembangunan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi rencana jangka panjang, rencana jangka menengah, dan rencana kerja pemerintah daerah.

# CHAPTER II

## WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

## Part One

General

#### Article 2

( 1 ) Women's empowerment in the Regency is implemented through the protection of women's rights.  

( 2 ) Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to fulfill women's rights in improving the quality of women's lives.  

( 3 ) Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (2) must be guaranteed by the Regency Government.  
8- ( 4 ) Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) include the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture, and social.

## Part Two

Obligations of the Regency Government

#### Article 3

( 1 ) The Regency Government is obligated to guarantee the protection of women's rights.  

( 2 ) Protection of women's rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. formulation of gender-responsive regional policies;  
b. institutionalization of PUG within the Regency Government;  
c. women's empowerment in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture, and social in community organizations at the Regency level; and  
d. strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency level.

#### Article 4

1. Formulation of gender-responsive Regency policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a serves as a guideline in the preparation of regional development plans.  
2. Preparation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (1) includes long-term plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans.  
3. Long-term development plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans as referred to in paragraph (2) must serve as a guideline for PD in the preparation of strategic plans and work plans within their respective working environments.  
4. Preparation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (3) is carried out through gender-responsive planning through gender analysis and ARG that contains a priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment.  
5. Preparation of the priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (4) is guided by the national level priority scale.  
9- (6) The national level priority scale as referred to in paragraph (5) becomes an inseparable part of the regional development plan.

#### Article 5

In order to ensure the realization of the formulation of gender-responsive policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a, PD that carry out governmental affairs in the field of regional development planning are obligated to:
a. involve PD that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment in the formulation of regional development plans; and  
b. evaluate programs and activities at the PD level that are not gender-responsive.

#### Article 6

1. Institutionalization of PUG as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter b is implemented in all PD within the Regency Government.  
2. To accelerate the institutionalization of PUG as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may establish a PUG Working Group at the Regency level.  
3. Members of the PUG Working Group as referred to in paragraph (2) are all Heads/Leaders of PD.  
4. Further provisions regarding the duties and procedures for membership of the PUG Working Group are regulated by Regent Regulation.

#### Article 7

( 1 ) In order to strengthen and develop PUG, the Regent may establish a PUG Focal Point.  

( 2 ) The PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) is a PD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.  

( 3 ) The Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) is established in each PD.  

( 4 ) Further provisions regarding the duties, membership composition and procedures for establishing the Focal Point are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
10-

#### Article 8

Women's empowerment in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, law, economy, culture, and social in community organizations at the Regency level as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter c constitutes part of temporary special policies provided by the Regency Government.

#### Article 9

Women's empowerment in the field of education is implemented by means including:
a. facilitating women to obtain education and teaching in all types, levels and pathways of education in accordance with predetermined requirements;  
b. education policies that encourage equity, improvement and quality relevance of education for all genders; and  
c. equitable learning opportunities for women and men.

#### Article 10

Women's empowerment in the field of health is implemented by means including:
a. facilitating women's health through health program activities implemented by the government such as:
1. Maternal mortality reduction program;  
2. Maternal and child health (KIA) program;  
3. Healthy environment, water sanitation and sanitation program;  
4. Malaria eradication program;  
5. Pulmonary tuberculosis eradication program;  
6. HIV/AIDS prevention program;  
7. Community nutrition improvement program;  
b. Women are given the right to obtain special protection in the implementation of their work or profession against matters that may threaten their safety and/or health;  
c. Women are given special rights inherent to women due to their reproductive function, guaranteed and protected by law.  
11-

#### Article 11

Women's empowerment in the field of employment is implemented by means including:
a. equal wages for male and female workers for the same work;  
b. prohibition of discrimination against female workers;  
c. prohibition of termination of employment for female workers who marry, become pregnant, and give birth;  
d. guidelines for employing female workers at night;  
e. providing flexibility for female workers who breastfeed children;  
f. prohibition of discrimination against female workers in company regulations; and  
g. regarding malnutrition in female workers.

#### Article 12

Women's empowerment in the field of politics is implemented by means including:
a. facilitating the improvement of human resources for prospective legislative candidates at the regency level, and members of political parties/women's community organizations in order to fulfill women's representation in legislative institutions in accordance with laws and regulations;  
b. facilitating increased political participation of women in legislative institutions;  
c. providing facilities and infrastructure for women's community organizations or community organizations whose vision and mission is to fight for the fulfillment of rights and protection of women in the Regency in accordance with Regional Financial capacity;  
d. implementing socialization in order to increase awareness of women's rights and women's participation in the field of politics;  
e. encouraging increased involvement of women in community organizations and decision-making activities within the Regency Government; and  
f. encouraging the establishment of women's organizations/forums.

#### Article 13

Women's empowerment in the field of law is implemented by means including:
a. facilitating the improvement of legal knowledge and awareness for women; and  
b. encouraging the establishment of organizations that provide free legal services for women.  
12-

#### Article 14

1. Women's empowerment in the field of economy is implemented by means including:
a. facilitating women in efforts to improve family economy;  
b. may provide capital assistance to women, especially migrant workers, women in remote areas, women as heads of households, and women victims of domestic violence; and  
c. implementing household industry and non-agricultural industry development programs.  
2. Procedures for providing capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Scope of Women's Empowerment

General

#### Article 17

b. provision of services and advanced referral handling; and  
c. strengthening and development of institutions providing women's protection services.

### Paragraph 2

Prevention

#### Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by means of increasing family and community awareness.  

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.  

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented by technical PD in charge, institutions, organizations, mass media, business world, academics, law enforcers, community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

#### Article 19

1. In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by increasing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.  
2. Prevention of violence against women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by means of:
a. increasing informal education;  
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement, and social services; and  
c. providing access to informal employment for women.

### Paragraph 3

Provision of Services and Advanced Referral Handling

#### Article 20

Provision of services and advanced referral handling as referred to in Article 17 letter b is intended for:
a. women victims of domestic violence;  
b. women victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons;  
c. women in emergency situations and special conditions; and  
d. women victims of other acts of violence requiring coordination at the Regency level.

#### Article 21

a. women who are included in vulnerable and/or minority groups;  
b. elderly women; and  
c. women with special needs.  
( 2 ) Special services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided in the form of:
a. ease in obtaining and enjoying their rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;  
b. ease in access to economic resources and natural resources, social security, and basic public services; and  
c. provision of specific needs of women in emergency situations and special conditions.

#### Article 41

Special protection for children from minority and isolated groups as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter c shall be carried out through the provision of facilities and infrastructure to enable them to enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and -26- practice their own religion, and use their own language.

#### Article 42

1. The provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out in the form of:
   a. provision of culture-based public spaces, art and culture centers, along with equipment and training including places of worship;  
   b. provision of facilities needed in providing services for Children from minority and isolated groups; and
   c. provision of accessibility needed by Children from minority and isolated groups to obtain fulfillment of basic needs.  
2. In the event that Children from minority and isolated groups experience trauma as a result of violence, discrimination and other mistreatment, they shall be provided with social rehabilitation, medical services, and/or mental health services.

#### Article 43

1. Special Protection for Children from Minority and Isolated Groups so that they do not experience violence, discrimination, and other mistreatment as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out through preventive measures.  
2. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
   a. provision of education to the community; and
   b. coordination with the Regency Government.
   c. preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
3. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 4

Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually

#### Article 44

Special Protection for Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out through:

a. dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations -27- relating to the protection of Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually;  
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children.

#### Article 45

1. Dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations as referred to in Article 44 letter a shall be carried out through:
   a. legal counseling; and
   b. communication, information, and education facilities.  
2. Dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.

#### Article 46

1. Monitoring as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be carried out by means of observation, identification, and recording to obtain data and information related to the condition of:
   a. children Who Are Exploited Economically; or
   b. children Who Are Exploited Sexually.  
2. Monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Economically as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out at economic center locations and outside economic centers.  
3. Monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Sexually as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out through supervision of:
   a. prostitution and solicitation practices in their environment;  
   b. locations suspected of being places of sexual exploitation of Children;  
   c. perpetrators suspected of sexually exploiting Children; and
   d. raid actions to free Children from sexual exploitation.  
4. Monitoring and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.  
5. Reporting as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be prepared after monitoring of Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually has been carried out.  
6. Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 44 -28- letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 47

Involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children as referred to in Article 44 letter c shall be carried out through:

a. formulation of policies on the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children in their environment;  
b. cooperation to prevent Children from being exploited economically and/or sexually;  
c. campaigns for the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children;  
d. increased supervision to prevent Children from being exploited economically and/or sexually;  
e. company support for the elimination of exploitation of Children through corporate social responsibility; and
f. reporting to the competent authorities if there is economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children.

#### Article 48

In the event that Children Who Are Exploited Economically and/or Sexually require restoration of their condition to its original state, they must be provided with services in the form of:

a. medical rehabilitation;  
b. Social rehabilitation;  
c. legal assistance and social assistance; and/or
d. repatriation and Social Reintegration.

### Paragraph 5

Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse

#### Article 49

Special Protection for Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter e shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts.

#### Article 50

Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out by means of: -29-

a. strengthening of families and the Community so that Children are no longer involved in the abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
b. monitoring in the surrounding environment to prevent the circulation or abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and
c. reporting to competent officials/agencies if there is circulation and abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

#### Article 51

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out through:

a. communication, information, and education about the dangers for Children if involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
b. enhancement of the role of parents, families, the Community, educators, education personnel, religious leaders, customary leaders, Community leaders in supporting the Social Reintegration process of Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse;  
c. provision of understanding and awareness to Children regarding the dangers of smoking;  
d. provision of understanding and awareness to Children about the dangers of Children being involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances;  
e. involvement of Children as peers in order to provide understanding and change of mindset about the dangers of Children being involved in the production and distribution as well as the dangers of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and
f. inclusion of anti-narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances teaching materials in education units.

#### Article 52

1. Treatment efforts as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out to provide recovery of the physical and psychological condition of Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substance Abuse.  
2. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
   a. outpatient care;  
   b. initial inpatient care;  
   c. follow-up care; and
   d. post-care.  
30-

#### Article 53

Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 49 shall be carried out through medical rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, and post-rehabilitation.

Children who are Victims of Pornography

#### Article 55

2. Provisions regarding guidance, assistance, social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

a. coordinating the prevention and handling of Child pornography;  
b. conducting socialization;  
c. organizing education and training;  
d. increasing public awareness and responsibility; and  
e. conducting guidance through institutional and non-institutional systems.

#### Article 57

Assistance as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be implemented through:

a. guidance and Counseling; and  
b. other necessary activities.

#### Article 58

Social recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:

a. resocialization;  
b. counseling on moral values sourced from religious teachings in accordance with the religion professed by the Child;  
c. increasing public awareness to be able to accept Children who are victims or perpetrators of pornography; and  
d. periodic monitoring.

#### Article 59

Physical and mental health recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:

a. psychosocial therapy;  
b. counseling;  
c. beneficial activities;  
d. referral to hospitals, safe houses, service centers, or other alternative places according to needs; and/or  
e. resocialization.

#### Article 60

1. Where necessary, the Regency Government and the Community may undertake prevention efforts so that Children do not become victims of pornography.  
2. Prevention efforts by the Regency Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:

a. formulation and implementation of policies related to regional action plans on the prevention and handling of pornography;  
b. optimization of the role of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Pornography;  
c. capacity building of the Regional Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Pornography;  
d. formulation and dissemination of communication, information, and education materials related to the prevention of pornography in schools and the Community;  
e. guidance to the Community not to engage in activities leading to pornography; and  
f. guidance to Regional Apparatus, non-governmental organizations, and the Community to enhance prevention and handling efforts for pornography.  
3. Prevention efforts by the Community so that Children do not become Victims of Pornography through:

a. dissemination of communication, information, and education materials related to the prevention of pornography in the surrounding environment;  
b. strengthening the surrounding environment not to engage in activities leading to pornography; and  
c. enhancing prevention and handling efforts for pornography in the surrounding environment.  
4. Provisions regarding the procedures for prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

#### Article 61

1. Guidance and assistance as referred to in Article 53 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its authority.  
2. Social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 7

Children with HIV and AIDS

#### Article 62

Special Protection for Children with HIV and AIDS as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter g shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, care, and rehabilitation efforts.

#### Article 63

Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 62 shall be carried out in the form of:

a. periodic or ad hoc examinations as well as integrated examinations of Children with HIV and AIDS;  
b. testing of periodic and/or ad hoc reports related to the prevention, handling, and protection of Children from HIV and AIDS;  
c. health surveillance in the form of recording, reporting, and data analysis on mothers, pregnant mothers, or Children indicated with HIV; and  
d. monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of prevention, handling, and protection of Children from HIV and AIDS.

#### Article 64

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 62 shall be carried out in the form of:

a. formulating and implementing policies related to action plans on the prevention and handling of Children with HIV and AIDS;  
b. health promotion to increase public knowledge about the benefits of early detection and transmission of HIV and AIDS as well as increasing the knowledge and responsibility of mothers, pregnant mothers, Children, and married couples;  
c. preventing the transmission of HIV and AIDS from mother to Child;  
d. preventing Children from using narcotics;  
e. early detection by providing HIV and AIDS tests to pregnant mothers in areas with widespread and concentrated HIV and AIDS endemics;  
f. early detection by providing HIV and AIDS tests to pregnant mothers with sexually transmitted infections and tuberculosis in low HIV epidemic areas;

Perlakuan Anak secara manusiawi sesuai dengan martabat dan hak Anak, pemenuhan kebutuhan khusus, perlakuan yang sama dengan Anak lainnya untuk mencapai integrasi sosial sepenuh mungkin dan pengembangan individu, dan Pendampingan Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 96 dilakukan sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang- undangan.

### Paragraf 13

Anak Korban Perlakuan Salah dan Penelantaran

#### Pasal 102

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak Korban Perlakuan Salah dan Anak Korban Penelantaran sebagaimana dimaksud dalamPasal 32 ayat (1) huruf m dilakukan melalui upaya pengawasan, pencegahan, perawatan, Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial.

#### Pasal 103

Pengawasan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 102 dilakukan dengan cara: -45-
a. pemetaan terhadap Anak yang rentan diperlakukan salah dan ditelantarkan; danb. diseminasi dan advokasi peraturan perundang- undangan.

#### Pasal 104

Pencegahan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 102 dilakukan dengan:
a. memberikan pembinaan kepada orang tua tentang hak Anak agar tidak diperlakukan salah dan ditelantarkan;  
b. memberikan layanan kebutuhan dasar;  
c. memberikan akses pendidikan; dand. memberikan pelatihan keterampilan atau kerja mandiri.

#### Pasal 105

Perawatan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 102 dilakukan dalam bentuk:
a. rehabilitasi medis; dan/ataub. pengasuhan keluarga atau Keluarga Pengganti untuk tumbuh kembang secara optimal.

#### Pasal 106

Ketentuan mengenai Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 83 berlaku secara mutatis mutandis terhadap bentuk Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 102.

#### Pasal 107

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak Korban Perlakuan Salah dan Penelantaran sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 102 dilakukan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten sesuai tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangannya.

### Paragraf 14

Anak Dengan Perilaku Sosial Menyimpang

#### Pasal 108

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak dengan Perilaku Sosial Menyimpang sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 32 ayat (1) huruf n dilakukan melalui bimbingan nilai agama dan nilai sosial, Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial.

#### Pasal 109

Bimbingan nilai agama dan nilai sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 108 diberikan dalam bentuk:
a. pengajaran untuk merijalankan perintah agama sesuai -46- keyakinan Anak dengan Perilaku Sosial yang Menyimpang;  
b. pemahaman untuk berperilaku sesuai dengan norma kesusilaan dan kesopanan;  
c. pemahaman untuk tidak melakukan kekerasan dan kerusakan; dand. peningkatan kepedulian terhadap lingkungan sekitar.

#### Pasal 110

Ketentuan mengenai Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 83 berlaku secara mutatis mutandis terhadap bentuk Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 108.

#### Pasal 111

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 108 dilakukan dengan melibatkan peran orang tua, Masyarakat, Lembaga Pendidikan, dan Lembaga Keagamaan.

#### Pasal 112

1. Bimbingan nilai agama dan nilai sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 109 dilakukan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.  
2. Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 108 dilakukan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.

### Paragraf 15

Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan Terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya

#### Pasal 113

Perlindungan Khusus bagi Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 32 ayat (1) huruf o dilakukan melalui Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial.

#### Pasal 114

Ketentuan mengenai Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 83 berlaku secara mutatis mutandis terhadap bentuk Rehabilitasi Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113.

#### Pasal 115

1. Anak yang telah mendapatkan Perlindungan Khusus sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113 dikembalikan -47- kepada keluarga atau Masyarakat.  
2. Sebelum dikembalikan kepada keluarga atau Masyarakat sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), langkah yang harus dilakukan:a. menyiapkan kondisi psikologis Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya untuk bersedia dikembalikan pada keluarga atau Masyarakat;  
b. memastikan keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat untuk menerima dan tidak lagi melakukan pelabelan dan diskriminasi terhadap Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya;  
c. menelusuri Keluarga Pengganti lain jika ada penolakan dari keluarga atau Masyarakat;  
d. memastikan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya dalam kondisi aman, nyaman, dan terpenuhi kebutuhannya; dane. melakukan pemantauan dan evaluasi perkembangan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya yang telah dikembalikan kepada keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat.

#### Pasal 116

Langkah pemantauan dan evaluasi perkembangan Anak yang Menjadi Korban Stigmatisasi dari Pelabelan terkait dengan Kondisi Orang Tuanya yang telah dikembalikan kepada keluarga, Keluarga Pengganti, atau Masyarakat sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 115 ayat (2) huruf e dilaksanakan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten sesuai dengan tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangannya.

#### Pasal 117

Konseling, Rehabilitasi Sosial, dan Pendampingan Sosial sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 113 dilakukan oleh Pemerintah Kabupaten sesuai dengan tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangannya.

#### Pasal 118

Untuk mencegah terjadinya stigmatisasi dari pelabelan terhadap Anak terkait kondisi orang tuanya, Pemerintah Kabupaten melakukan:
a. pemberian edukasi kepada Masyarakat serta berperan aktif untuk menghilangkan stigma terhadap Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi orang tuanya;  

b.pemberian ruang kepada Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi -48- orang tuanya untuk mendapatkan kegiatan rekreasional; dan
c. koordinasi dengan unit layanan yang menangani perlindungan Anak yang dilabeli terkait kondisi orang tuanya dalam hal terdapat potensi kekerasan dan diskriminasi terhadap Anak di Kabupaten.

## Bagian Keempat

Layanan atau Penanganan Rujukan Lanjutan bagi Anak Korban Kekerasan

#### Pasal 119

Dalam rangka perlindungan anak, Pemerintah Kabupaten berkewajiban:
a. menyediakan layanan atau penanganan rujukan lanjutan; danb. melakukan penguatan dan pengembangan lembaga penyedialayanan perlindungan perempuan dan anak.

#### Pasal 120

( 1 ) Penyediaan layanan atau penanganan rujukan lanjutan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 119 huruf a diperuntukkan bagi anak korban kekerasan yang memerlukan koordinasi tingkat Kabupaten.  

( 2 ) Penyediaaan layanan atau penanganan rujukan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan melalui unit PPA tingkat Kabupaten.  

( 3 ) Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai tugas, keanggaotaan, dan pembentukan unit PPA sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

# BAB IV

## PENINGKATAN KUALITAS KELUARGA

#### Pasal 121

Peningkatan kualitas keluarga dilaksanakan dalam rangka mewujudkan kesetaraan gender dan hak anak.

#### Pasal 122

Peningkatan kualitas keluarga dilakukan melalui: a. pencegahan perkawinan usia anak;  
b. pemenuhan hak anak atas ASI eksklusif;  
c. mendekatkan ibu pada pelayanan kesehatan;  
d. meningkatkan ketahanan keluarga.  
49-

#### Pasal 123

Pencegahan perkawinan usia anak sebagaimana dimaksud dalamPasal 122 huruf a bertujuan:
a. meningkatkan produkstivitas anak perempuan; b. mengembangkan potensi diri anak perempuan; c. mencegah kehamilan di usia terlalu muda;  
d. menurunkan angka kematian ibu dan bayi;  
e. menurunkan angka kemiskinan; danf. mencegah terjadinya kekerasan dalam rumah tangga.

#### Article 101

Humane treatment of Children in accordance with the dignity and rights of the Child, fulfillment of special needs, equal treatment with other Children to achieve the fullest possible social integration and individual development, and Social Assistance as referred to in Article 96 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 13

Children Victims of Maltreatment and Neglect

#### Article 102

Special Protection for Children Victims of Maltreatment and Children Victims of Neglect as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter m shall be carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, care, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance.

#### Article 103

Supervision as referred to in Article 102 shall be carried out by way of:

a. mapping of Children who are vulnerable to maltreatment and neglect; and
b. dissemination and advocacy of laws and regulations.

#### Article 104

Prevention as referred to in Article 102 shall be carried out by:

a. providing guidance to parents regarding the rights of Children not to be maltreated and neglected;  
b. providing basic needs services;  
c. providing access to education; and
d. providing skills training or independent work.

#### Article 105

Care as referred to in Article 102 shall be carried out in the form of:

a. medical rehabilitation; and/or
b. family care or Substitute Family for optimal growth and development.

#### Article 106

The provisions regarding Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the form of Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 102.

#### Article 107

Special Protection for Children Victims of Maltreatment and Neglect as referred to in Article 102 shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.

### Paragraph 14

Children With Deviant Social Behavior

#### Article 108

Special Protection for Children with Deviant Social Behavior as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter n shall be carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance.

#### Article 109

Guidance on religious values and social values as referred to in Article 108 shall be provided in the form of:

a. teaching to carry out religious commands in accordance with the beliefs of Children with Deviant Social Behavior;  
b. understanding to behave in accordance with norms of decency and propriety;  
c. understanding not to commit violence and destruction; and
d. increasing awareness of the surrounding environment.

#### Article 110

The provisions regarding Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the form of Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 108.

#### Article 111

Special Protection for Children as referred to in Article 108 shall be carried out by involving the role of parents, the Community, Educational Institutions, and Religious Institutions.

#### Article 112

1. Guidance on religious values and social values as referred to in Article 109 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.  
2. Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance as referred to in Article 108 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

### Paragraph 15

Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling Related to the Condition of Their Parents

#### Article 113

Special Protection for Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter o shall be carried out through Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance.

#### Article 114

The provisions regarding Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the form of Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 113.

#### Article 115

1. Children who have received Special Protection as referred to in Article 113 shall be returned to their family or the Community.  
2. Before being returned to the family or the Community as referred to in paragraph (1), the steps that must be taken are:

a. preparing the psychological condition of Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents to be willing to be returned to the family or the Community;  
b. ensuring the family, Substitute Family, or the Community to accept and no longer label and discriminate against Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents;  
c. tracing another Substitute Family if there is rejection from the family or the Community;  
d. ensuring Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are in a safe, comfortable condition, and their needs are met; and

e. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the development of Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents who have been returned to the family, Substitute Family, or the Community.

#### Article 116

The steps for monitoring and evaluation of the development of Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents who have been returned to the family, Substitute Family, or the Community as referred to in Article 115 paragraph (2) letter e shall be implemented by the Regency Government in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.

#### Article 117

Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance as referred to in Article 113 shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.

#### Article 118

To prevent the occurrence of stigmatization from labeling of Children related to the condition of their parents, the Regency Government shall:

a. provide education to the Community and play an active role in eliminating stigma against Children who are labeled related to the condition of their parents;  

b. provide space for Children who are labeled related to the condition of their parents to obtain recreational activities; and
c. coordinate with service units that handle the protection of Children who are labeled related to the condition of their parents in the event of potential violence and discrimination against Children in the Regency.

## Part Four

Referral Services or Further Handling for Child Victims of Violence

#### Article 119

In the context of child protection, the Regency Government is obligated to:

a. provide referral services or further handling; and
b. strengthen and develop institutions providing protection services for women and children.

#### Article 120

( 1 ) The provision of referral services or further handling as referred to in Article 119 letter a shall be intended for child victims of violence who require coordination at the Regency level.  

( 2 ) The provision of referral services or handling as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the PPA unit at the Regency level.  

( 3 ) Further provisions regarding the duties, membership, and establishment of the PPA unit as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

# CHAPTER IV

## IMPROVING FAMILY QUALITY

#### Article 121

Improving family quality shall be implemented in order to realize gender equality and children's rights.

#### Article 122

Improving family quality shall be carried out through:

a. prevention of child marriage;  
b. fulfillment of children's rights to exclusive breastfeeding;  
c. bringing mothers closer to health services;  
d. increasing family resilience.

#### Article 123

Prevention of child marriage as referred to in Article 122 letter a aims to:

a. increase the productivity of girls;  
b. develop the potential of girls;  
c. prevent pregnancy at too young an age;  
d. reduce maternal and infant mortality rates;  
e. reduce poverty rates; and
f. prevent the occurrence of domestic violence.

Pemenuhan hak anak atas ASI eksklusif sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 123 huruf b bertujuan:
a. menjamin hak setiap anak memperoleh ASI eksklusif;  
b. menjamin kesehatan anak dan tumbuh kembang secara optimal, terutama pada usia emas; danc. mencegah gizi buruk.

#### Pasal 125

Mendekatkan ibu pada pelayanan kesehatan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 122 huruf c bertujuan:
a. menjamin kesehatan ibu dan anak baik sebelum, pada saat, maupun pasca melahirkan; danb. meningkatkan wawasan dan pengetahuan ibu tentang kesehatan diri dan keluarga.

#### Pasal 126

Ketahanan keluarga sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 122 huruf d bertujuan:
a. memenuhi hak anggota keluarga;  
b. meningkatan kualitas hidup anggota keluarga; dan c. meningkatkan kesejahteraan keluarga.

#### Pasal 127

Ketentuan lebih lanjut mengenai bentuk kegiatan dan tata cara pelaksanaan peningkatan kualitas keluarga sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 122 diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

# BAB V

## SISTEM DATA GENDER DAN ANAK

#### Pasal 128

1. Pemerintah Kabupaten menyelenggarakan sisteminformasi data gender dan anak.  
50- (2) Pemerintah Kabupaten membentuk forum/kelompok kerja sistem data gender dan anak yang diatur dalamPeraturan Bupati.  

3. Dalam rangka pembentukan tim, penyusunan pengumpulan, pengolahan, analisis dan penyajian data gender dan anak, Pemerintah Kabupaten berkoordinasi dengan PD terkait di tingkat kabupaten.  
4. Penyajian Data gender dan anak dikembangkan dalamaplikasi sistem informasi keluarga dan e-kekerasan.  
5. Penyajian dan pemanfaatan data gender dan anak digunakan dalam percepatan pelaksana PUG dalampembangunan daerah.  
6. Ketentuan lebih lanjut tentang pelaksanaan sisteminformasi data gender dan anak sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

# BAB VI

## KOORDINASI DAN KERJA SAMA

#### Pasal 129

1. Pemerintah Kabupaten membentuk forum koordinasi dan kerjasama dalam penyelenggarakan perlindungan perempuan dan anak dengan:a. Pemerintah Kabupaten lain; dan/ataub. lembaga/instansi lainnya.  
2. Koordinator pelaksanaan koordinasi dan kerjasama penyelenggaran perlindungan perempuan dan anak dikoordinasikan oleh PD yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang Perlindungan Anak.  
3. Ketentuan lebih lanjut tentang pembentukan tata cara forum sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati.

#### Pasal 130

Dalam rangka koordinasi pelaksanaan perlindungan perempuan dan anak, Pemerintah Kabupaten dapat membangun jejaring dan kerja sama dengan aparatur penegak hukum, aparatur pemerintah, perguruan tinggi dan berbagai lembaga swadaya masyarakat bergerak dan/atau peduli terhadap perempuan.

# BAB VII

## PARTISIPASI MASYARAKAT

#### Pasal 131

1. Masyarakat dapat berpartisipasi dalam penyelenggaraan perlindungan perempuan dan perlindungan anak.  
2. Partisipasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dapat dilaksanakan dalam rangka pencegahan, penanganan dan pemberdayaan, dan pemenuhan hak anak.  
3. Peran masyarakat dalam penyelenggaraan perlindungan anak sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan dengan cara:a. memberikan informasi melalui sosialisasi dan edukasi mengenai hak anak dan peraturan perundang- undangan tentang anak;  
b. memberikan masukan dalam perumusan kebijakan yang terkait perlindungan anak;  
c. melaporkan kepada pihak yang berwenang jika terjadi pelanggaran hak anak;  
d. berperan aktif dalam proses rehabilitasi dan reintegrasi sosial bagi anak;  
e. melakukan pemantauan, pengawasan dan ikutbertanggung jawab terhadap penyelenggaraan perlindungan anak;  
f. menyediakan sarana dan prasarana serta menciptakan suasana kondusif untuk tumbuh kembang anak;  
g. membentuk forum koordinasi wilayah Kabupaten;  
h. berperan aktif dengan menghilangkan pelabelan negatif terhadap Anak; dani. memberikan ruang kepada anak untuk dapat berpartisipasi dan menyampaikan pendapatnya.  
4. Peran organisasi kemasyarakatan dan lembaga pendidikan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) dilakukan dengan cara mengambil langkah yang diperlukan sesuai tugas, fungsi, dan kewenangan masing-masing untuk membantu penyelenggaraan perlindungan anak serta pemberiaan informasi.  
5. Peran media massa sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) dilakukan melalui penyebarluasan informasi dan materi edukasi yang bermanfaat dari aspek sosial, budaya, pendidikan, agama dan kesehatan anak dengan memperhatikan kepentingan terbaik bagi Anak.  
6. Peran dunia usaha sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2) dilakukan melalui:a. kebijakan perusahaan yang berperspektif anak;  
52-
b. produk yang ditunjukan untuk anak harus aman bagi anak; danc. berkontribusi dalam pemenuhan hak anak melalui tanggung jawab sosial perusahaan.

#### Pasal 132

Dalam rangka penguatan dan pengembangan layanan bagi anak korban kekerasan, masyarakat atau lembaga pelayanan sosial dapat membentuk fasilitas khusus.

# BAB VIII

## PEMBINAAN DAN PENGAWASAN

#### Pasal 133

1. Bupati berkewajiban melakukan pembinaan terhadap penyelenggaraan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak.  
2. Pelaksanaan pembinaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan oleh PD yang menyelenggarakan urusanpemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak.  
3. Pembinaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), meliputi:a. pedoman dan standar pemenuhan;  
b. bimbingan teknis dan pelatihan;  
c. penyediaan fasilitas;  
d. pemantauan; dane. evaluasi.  
4. Pengawasan dilaksanakan dalam bentuk:a. pemantauan; danb. evaluasi.  
5. Dalam melaksanakan pembinaan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1), PD yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak dapat bekerja sama dan berkoordinasi dengan PD lain di lingkungan Pemerintah Kabupaten atau instansi/lembaga lain yang terkait di Kabupaten.

#### Pasal 134

1. Bupati berkewajiban melakukan pengawasan terhadap penyelenggaraan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak.  
2. Pelaksanaan pengawasan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan oleh PD yang menyelenggarakan fungsi pengawasan.  
53-

#### Pasal 135

1. Selain PD yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak, untuk menjamin efektivitas pelaksanaan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak di Kabupaten, setiap PD berkewajiban melakukan pengawasan dalam bentuk pemantauan dan evaluasi.  
2. Pengawasan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan secara berjenjang sesuai dengan kewenangan masing-masing.  
3. Hasil pemantauan dan evaluasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) diumumkan kepada masyarakat.

#### Pasal 136

1. Laporan hasil pembinaan dan pengawasan disampaikan kepada bupati.  
2. Pelaporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan paling lama setiap 6 (enam) bulan sekali.  
3. Pelaporan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan secara berjejaring atau antar PD, dan dikoordinasi oleh PDyang menyelenggarakan urusan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan perempuan dan anak.

# BAB IX

## PENDANAAN

#### Pasal 137

Pendanaan pelaksanaan pemberdayaan perempuan dan perlindungan anak bersumber dari:
a. anggaran pendapatan dan belanja daerah; danb. sumber lain yang sah, sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.

# BAB X

## LARANGAN

#### Pasal 138

Setiap penyelenggara pendidikan di tingkat kabupaten dilarang:
a. membuat tata tertib sekolah yang berpotensi melanggar hak anak; dan/atau -54-b. mengeluarkan Anak dari lembaga pendidikan tanpa adanya jaminan terhadap keberlangsungan pendidikan Anak.

# BAB XI

## SANKSI ADMINISTRATIF

#### Pasal 139

1. Pimpinan satuan pendidikan yang melanggar ketentuan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 138 dapat dikenakan sanksi administrasi.  
2. Sanksi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dapat berupa:a. peringatan tertulis;  
b. mutasi;  
c. penurunan pangkat;  
d. pemberhentian dari jabatan; ataue. pencabutan izin.  
3. Pengenaan sanksi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanaa sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang- undangan.

#### Article 124

The fulfillment of children's rights to exclusive breastfeeding as referred to in Article 123 letter b aims to:
a. guarantee the right of every child to obtain exclusive breastfeeding;  
b. guarantee the health of children and optimal growth and development, especially during the golden age; and  
c. prevent malnutrition.

#### Article 125

Bringing mothers closer to health services as referred to in Article 122 letter c aims to:
a. guarantee the health of mothers and children before, during, and after childbirth; and  
b. increase mothers' insight and knowledge about their own health and that of their families.

#### Article 126

Family resilience as referred to in Article 122 letter d aims to:
a. fulfill the rights of family members;  
b. improve the quality of life of family members; and  
c. improve family welfare.

#### Article 127

Further provisions regarding the form of activities and procedures for implementing family quality improvement as referred to in Article 122 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

# CHAPTER V

## GENDER AND CHILD DATA SYSTEM

#### Article 128

1. The Regency Government organizes a gender and child data information system.

2. The Regency Government establishes a forum/working group for the gender and child data system as regulated in the Regent Regulation.  

3. In the context of forming a team, compiling, collecting, processing, analyzing and presenting gender and child data, the Regency Government coordinates with relevant Regional Apparatus at the regency level.  
4. The presentation of gender and child data is developed in a family information system application and e-violence.  
5. The presentation and utilization of gender and child data is used in accelerating the implementation of Gender Mainstreaming in regional development.  
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of the gender and child data information system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

# CHAPTER VI

## COORDINATION AND COOPERATION

#### Article 129

1. The Regency Government establishes a coordination and cooperation forum in organizing the protection of women and children with:
a. other Regency Governments; and/or  
b. other institutions/agencies.  
2. The coordinator for the implementation of coordination and cooperation in organizing the protection of women and children is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that organizes governmental affairs in the field of Child Protection.  
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment of forum procedures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

#### Article 130

In the context of coordinating the implementation of the protection of women and children, the Regency Government may build networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that are active and/or care about women.

# CHAPTER VII

## COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

#### Article 131

1. The community may participate in organizing the protection of women and the protection of children.  
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be implemented in the context of prevention, handling and empowerment, and fulfillment of children's rights.  
3. The role of the community in organizing child protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing information through socialization and education regarding children's rights and laws and regulations concerning children;  
b. providing input in the formulation of policies related to child protection;  
c. reporting to the competent authorities if violations of children's rights occur;  
d. playing an active role in the rehabilitation and social reintegration process for children;  
e. conducting monitoring, supervision and being jointly responsible for the organization of child protection;  
f. providing facilities and infrastructure and creating a conducive atmosphere for the growth and development of children;  
g. forming a Regency area coordination forum;  
h. playing an active role in eliminating negative labeling of Children; and  
i. providing space for children to participate and express their opinions.  
4. The role of community organizations and educational institutions as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by taking the necessary steps in accordance with their respective duties, functions, and authorities to assist in organizing child protection and providing information.  
5. The role of mass media as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from the social, cultural, educational, religious and health aspects of children with due regard to the best interests of the Child.  
6. The role of the business world as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out through:
a. child-perspective corporate policies;  
52-

b. products intended for children must be safe for children; and  
c. contributing to the fulfillment of children's rights through corporate social responsibility.

#### Article 132

In the context of strengthening and developing services for child victims of violence, the community or social service institutions may establish special facilities.

# CHAPTER VIII

## GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

#### Article 133

1. The Regent is obliged to provide guidance on the organization of women's empowerment and child protection.  
2. The implementation of guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that organizes the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection.  
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;  
b. technical guidance and training;  
c. provision of facilities;  
d. monitoring; and  
e. evaluation.  
4. Supervision is implemented in the form of:
a. monitoring; and  
b. evaluation.  
5. In carrying out guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that organizes the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus within the Regency Government or other related agencies/institutions in the Regency.

#### Article 134

1. The Regent is obliged to supervise the organization of women's empowerment and child protection.  
2. The implementation of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs the supervisory function.

#### Article 135

1. In addition to the Regional Apparatus that organizes the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection, to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Regency, every Regional Apparatus is obliged to conduct supervision in the form of monitoring and evaluation.  
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a tiered manner in accordance with their respective authorities.  
3. The results of monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be announced to the public.

#### Article 136

1. Reports on the results of guidance and supervision shall be submitted to the regent.  
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out at least once every 6 (six) months.  
3. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in a networked manner or between Regional Apparatus, and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that organizes the affairs of women's empowerment and the protection of women and children.

# CHAPTER IX

## FUNDING

#### Article 137

Funding for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and  
b. other lawful sources, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

# CHAPTER X

## PROHIBITIONS

#### Article 138

Every education organizer at the regency level is prohibited from:
a. making school rules that have the potential to violate children's rights; and/or  
b. expelling Children from educational institutions without guarantees for the continuity of the Child's education.

# CHAPTER XI

## ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

#### Article 139

1. The head of an education unit who violates the provisions as referred to in Article 138 may be subject to administrative sanctions.  
2. Sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. written warning;  
b. transfer;  
c. demotion;  
d. dismissal from position; or  
e. revocation of license.  
3. The imposition of sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
